nodes.label: Authority Boundary
nodes.rationale: The daemon has no authentication, so an unguarded bridge would hand an LLM the ability to spawn PTY processes anywhere; coven-mcp denies writes by default and authorizes against the daemon's own session records rather than caller-supplied paths.

nodes.label: Upstream Behaviors
nodes.rationale: Five load-bearing daemon behaviors (camelCase events envelope, undocumented kill event kind, bare-array vs envelope responses, string-valued capabilities, covenVersion 0.0.0) were verified against the live daemon rather than assumed from docs, because upstream ships ~10 commits/day and four daemon doc pages are one-line stubs.

nodes.label: Architecture Decisions
nodes.rationale: TypeScript/Node 22 is the fastest path at this budget (Rust not worth the hours); stdio transport gives simplest client config with no network surface; node:http with socketPath because the daemon is HTTP over a Unix socket; no streaming because no push transport exists (coven-relay is a stub); Windows and semantic memory are out of scope because named-pipe transport is undocumented and coven-memory is unreachable over the socket.

nodes.label: Known Traps
nodes.rationale: Fifteen pre-loaded upstream quirks (mixed casing conventions, double-encoded payload_json, raw PTY output, undocumented kill event, 4 MiB socket body cap, bare-array/envelope pagination, resume tokens dying on MCP client restarts) recorded so they are not rediscovered as bugs during the build window.

nodes.label: V1 Tool Surface
nodes.rationale: Nine tools locked to daemon routes; token streaming, Windows, semantic memory search, hub/scheduler/travel routes, and POST /actions explicitly cut because honest scope reads as maturity.

nodes.label: Security Design
nodes.rationale: The daemon has no authentication, so the MCP server inherits full same-user authority; most entrants will ship this unguarded, so ~2 hours of allowlist gating, fail-loud misconfiguration, excerpt redaction, and a documented threat model buys both the security score and differentiation.

nodes.label: Checkpoint A
nodes.rationale: Hard abort gate at ~6h: a bridge that half-connects scores below a linter that works, so failure means immediate descope to the Familiar Contract validator rather than pushing through.

nodes.label: Descope Ladder
nodes.rationale: Ordered cuts if behind schedule: memory tool first, then event accumulation (return raw events), then write tools (ship a read-only observability bridge that still demos, is still novel, and still honest).

nodes.label: Freeze Checklist
nodes.rationale: Friday is freeze day, not build day; scripts/freeze-preflight.mjs mechanizes the checklist because a wrong tag name is unrecoverable after the deadline.

nodes.label: Documentation Contract
nodes.rationale: The official submission guide specifies 14 exact README section headings in order; npm run verify enforces them mechanically so the docs check can never silently drift from the guide.

nodes.label: coven_read_output
nodes.rationale: The hardest component: bounded polling of the events route with a streaming sanitizer state machine, because output.data is raw PTY text with ANSI escapes split across events, payload_json is double-encoded JSON, and every stop must map to exactly one documented tuple so callers can branch deterministically.

nodes.label: Resume Token
nodes.rationale: HMAC-SHA-256-signed base64url payload {v, sessionId, afterSeq, pendingRawB64}; null afterSeq is the explicit pre-first-event state so no sentinel is invented; pending state is compacted (current line + incomplete escape) so a CR-heavy progress bar can never grow state unboundedly; UTF-16LE encoding so a chunk split inside a surrogate pair survives; per-process secret means tokens intentionally die on restart, with afterSeq=lastSeq as the documented recovery.

nodes.label: Authority Boundary
nodes.rationale: Deny by default (unset allowlist means read-only); misconfiguration aborts startup loudly rather than degrading; write tools authorize the daemon's canonical project_root, never a caller-supplied path; containment is path-component based after symlink resolution; the allowlist is an authorization gate, not a sandbox, and prompt injection is explicitly in the threat model.

nodes.label: Error Taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Branch on error.code, never message text; only named daemon codes get bespoke handling and the other ~33 fall through to structured UPSTREAM_ERROR so unmapped codes can never become transport errors or leak raw daemon bodies.

nodes.label: Health Gate
nodes.rationale: Lazy per-call handshake (cached 1.5s, single-flight) instead of a startup check, so tool discovery stays stable while the daemon is down and daemon restarts never require restarting the MCP client; a capability counts only when exactly true because health advertises string-valued capabilities.

nodes.label: Memory Excerpt Policy
nodes.rationale: The daemon route includes bounded excerpts, so blindly forwarding it is content disclosure; excerpts are blanked by default, forwarded only under COVEN_MCP_INCLUDE_MEMORY_EXCERPTS=true, and revealRequired or non-public classification forces redaction even then.

nodes.label: coven-mcp
nodes.rationale: Bridges the Coven daemon to stdio MCP clients because Coven state is otherwise invisible from Claude Desktop/Cursor, forcing context-switching that defeats the point of an agent runtime; additive to coven-reach and coven-codeflow rather than competing.

nodes.label: coven_health
nodes.rationale: Never fails: an unreachable daemon is reported as data, not a tool error, so it stays useful as a diagnostic when everything else is failing.

nodes.label: coven_list_memory
nodes.rationale: A file lister, not search or content read, because the daemon route accepts no filters; advertising unsupported filters would be dishonest scope.

nodes.label: coven_send_input
nodes.rationale: Forwards data to the PTY verbatim with no appended newline, so callers must include a trailing newline to submit a line — rewriting input would make the bridge lossy.

nodes.label: COVEN_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS
nodes.rationale: Colon-separated absolute roots gating all write tools; unset means read-only; any invalid entry aborts startup naming its position (never its value) so a misconfigured allowlist is never partially honored; containment is path-component based after symlink resolution so /work/app2 is never inside /work/app.

nodes.label: Resume Token
nodes.rationale: HMAC-signed with a random per-process secret, session-bound and size-capped; integrity-protected but not encrypted since the payload includes un-emitted output state, so tokens must be treated as session output and never logged.

nodes.label: ANSI/CR Sanitizer
nodes.rationale: Raw PTY output (ANSI escapes, carriage-return progress bars, lines split across events) is reassembled into plain text because the consumer is an LLM, not a terminal emulator.

nodes.label: Capability Handshake
nodes.rationale: Every non-health call requires ok===true, apiVersion coven.daemon.v1, and the needed capability advertised as exactly true; string capabilities are diagnostic only, and the legacy /api/v1/api-version route is deliberately unused because upstream documents it as not proof of support.

nodes.label: Trust Model
nodes.rationale: Daemon trust is same-user socket access with no authentication, so coven-mcp inherits full same-user authority and its job is to narrow it before an LLM touches it; the allowlist is authorization not a sandbox; tool results are untrusted content with respect to prompt injection (encoding sanitized, meaning not); anyone with same-user access can bypass coven-mcp entirely.

nodes.label: Verify Pipeline
nodes.rationale: npm run verify needs no credentials, daemon, or network so a judge can prove the package from a clean clone in seconds; contract tests bind a real HTTP server to a temporary Unix socket rather than mocking node:http internals.

nodes.label: Demo
nodes.rationale: npm run demo drives the real built server over real MCP stdio against a scripted stand-in daemon: deterministic, no credentials or provider spend, so the demo artifact works for judges without a Coven install.

nodes.label: normalize.ts
nodes.rationale: The single snake_case-to-camelCase boundary plus the memory excerpt redaction policy — normalization lives in one module so upstream casing quirks cannot leak into tool code.

nodes.label: read-output.ts
nodes.rationale: Bounded polling reader with cursor guards and budgets; invariants: an event is consumed only once its text and pending state fit the budget (try before commit), a terminal session completes only after one further empty drain so racing trailing output is never dropped, and an error never discards text already produced.

nodes.label: sanitizer.ts
nodes.rationale: Eight-state terminal state machine that emits only on a newline reached in ground state so a split escape sequence can never leak; carriage return overwrites from line start so progress bars collapse to final state; pending state is compacted, never accumulated raw history, so a long-running progress bar cannot grow state without bound.

nodes.label: errors.ts
nodes.rationale: The only shared leaf in the module graph; nothing else fans in, keeping the dependency graph acyclic and shallow.

nodes.label: Request Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Every tool call runs the same six stages (schema validation, health gate, authorization, transport, normalization/output pipeline, result shaping); stages 1-3 can reject without touching the daemon, which is what makes Guards a trust boundary.

nodes.label: Security Model
nodes.rationale: Narrowing the authority an LLM inherits is the point of the project, not a feature of it; controls are deny-by-default, fail-fast configuration, authoritative-record authorization, path-component containment, fail-closed lookups, excerpt redaction, and no sensitive logging — while explicitly not guaranteeing a sandbox, semantic sanitization, token encryption, or protection from same-user bypass.

nodes.label: Upstream Contract
nodes.rationale: Pinned to OpenCoven/coven 1fe9a744 (CLI 0.0.34); six live-verified behaviors are each absorbed at a single boundary module so they cannot leak into tool code.
